chapter_intro: Jeremiah’s Struggles with God and Judah.

passages.title: Jeremiah’s Struggles with God and Judah.
passages.text: As the nation faces invasion, Jeremiah struggles to serve God faithfully. He is surprised by opposition (11:1–12:17), stunned over feeling betrayed by God (13:1–15:21), renewed by God (16:1–17:18), burdened by opposition (17:19–18:23), and prepared to continue serving (19:1–20:18).

notes.text: drought. Judah experiences drought during the invasion by Babylon (see Deut. 28:23–24).
Jeremiah intercedes, recognizing Judah’s rebellion and spiritual unfaithfulness (see Amos 7:1–9).
we are called by your name. God has been Israel’s deliverer in the past. Jeremiah wonders if God will help the nation for the sake of his reputation (Lam. 1:20–22; 2:20–22).

God is able to save, but Israel’s constant unfaithfulness must be addressed. For God remembering his people’s iniquity and sins, see Hos. 7:2; 8:13; and contrast Ps. 25:7; 79:8; Isa. 43:25; Jer. 31:34.
Sword and famine. Babylon and the drought (compare 11:22–23).
Why have you struck us? Jeremiah questions God again, declaring that the people were misled. He wonders if God has rejected them (see Lam. 5:22).
Jeremiah expresses his faith on behalf of Judah, but the people do not share his convictions, as God knows. remember. See v. 10.
